Customers are advised to disconnect from networks and power down systems as a precaution against imminent encryption threats.

cards.headline: Convertr analytics script hijacked for payment card theft
cards.summary: Attackers compromised a shared analytics script used by e-commerce platform Convertr to steal payment card data from shoppers during checkout. The hijacked script allowed attackers to intercept sensitive payment information from multiple merchants using the platform. Organizations using Convertr should audit transactions and implement payment security monitoring.

cards.headline: Ukrainian ransomware affiliate sentenced to 70 months prison
cards.summary: Artem Aleksandrovych Stryzhak, 36, was sentenced to 70 months in prison for participating in ransomware attacks from 2018 to 2021. He affiliated with Nefilim and Hive ransomware groups, targeting approximately 1,500 victims including hospitals, government entities, and critical infrastructure operators. His attacks disrupted patient care and caused millions in damages. Stryzhak was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the U.S. in April 2025.

cards.headline: CyberStrikeAI uses 44 AI agents targeting Japanese organizations
cards.summary: Researchers at TrendAI discovered three cyber attacks against Japanese organizations where threat actors leveraged 44 AI agents to automate hacking operations. The attacks involved either AI-driven autonomous operations or AI-assisted human-led campaigns. Three exposed server environments used by the threat actors were analyzed. The disclosure details how adversaries are increasingly adopting AI to scale and accelerate cyber attack capabilities.

cards.headline: Microsoft removes trust in compromised eMudhra certificates
cards.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band Windows updates to distrust certificates issued by eMudhra certificate authority after compromised keys were discovered. The emergency patches protect systems that do not automatically receive certificate trust updates from potential man-in-the-middle attacks. Organizations running affected Windows versions should apply the updates promptly to prevent threat actors from using fraudulent certificates.

cards.headline: Aokigahara stealer targets developer keys and AI assistants
cards.summary: Aokigahara infostealer malware expands beyond traditional credential theft to target developer keyrings and AI assistant sessions. A single compromised endpoint can expose sensitive business data, AI sessions, and developer infrastructure. The malware represents an escalation of infostealer capabilities in the era of AI-assisted development. Organizations should monitor for signs of compromise and review access to AI platforms and developer credentials.

cards.headline: Warp agentic platform breached, agent logs exposed
cards.summary: Warp, an agentic development environment, suffered a breach through a compromised third-party vendor in its infrastructure. Attackers accessed agent decision logs and user telemetry data from Warp users. The incident highlights supply-chain risks in AI development tooling. Users should review logs for suspicious activity and monitor accounts for unauthorized access.

cards.headline: Tailscale Tailworm SSH flaws disclosed before patches ready
cards.summary: Tailscale security flaws dubbed 'Tailworm' affecting SSH were disclosed publicly over the weekend without coordinated vendor notification, forcing the company to rush patch development. Details went public before fixes were available, creating a window of exposure. Users should prioritize applying patches immediately when released and monitor for unusual Tailscale SSH activity on their networks.

cards.headline: UK police data breached repeatedly through third-party suppliers
cards.summary: British police information was compromised multiple times over the past decade via breaches at third-party IT suppliers, according to His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services. The watchdog investigation found recurring security failures among contractors holding sensitive law enforcement data. Organizations should audit their supply chain security controls and enforce strict access policies for third-party vendors handling restricted information.

cards.headline: GoAhead web server TLS flaws bypass certificate revocation
cards.summary: GoAhead embedded web server contains TLS flaws affecting systems configured with mutual-TLS authentication. The server loads certificate revocation lists but never enables revocation checking, allowing revoked client certificates to pass authentication. Session decryption is also possible. Organizations using GoAhead with OpenSSL backend and mutual-TLS should verify revocation checking is enabled or disable affected configurations.

cards.headline: Apple backports CoreGraphics RCE fix to older iPhones
cards.summary: Apple backported patches for CVE-2026-86950, a high-severity out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics affecting older iPhones and iPads. The flaw allows arbitrary code execution when processing malicious files and has been exploited in real-world attacks. Patches released last month are now available for older devices. Users should update immediately to the latest available iOS version.

cards.headline: Infostealers disguised as Russian gas price tracking apps
cards.summary: Cybercriminals deployed infostealer malware in fake applications targeting Russians, posing as tools for tracking fuel prices, police activity and drone strike information. The malware steals sensitive data from infected devices. Users should avoid downloading apps from untrusted sources and verify app legitimacy before installation. Organizations should warn employees about these threats.

cards.headline: Leaked SquareML key exposes 238k Denver Health Plan members
cards.summary: A SquareML access key exposure put personal and health information of 238,000 Denver Health Plan members at risk. The breach occurred via compromised credentials that could have enabled unauthorized database access. Denver Health Plan has been notified and is investigating the incident. Organizations should audit access keys and implement key rotation protocols to prevent similar incidents.

cards.headline: Microsoft Authenticator Android flaw steals work account tokens
cards.summary: Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-80097, a vulnerability in Authenticator for Android that allowed malicious apps with no permissions to impersonate trusted Microsoft apps like Teams and steal work account sign-in tokens. The flaw was patched in Authenticator version 6.2606.4246. Users should update immediately to prevent unauthorized access to work accounts and sensitive resources.

cards.headline: Keystone to destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after key theft
cards.summary: Keystone announced it will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after attackers obtained the device verification key from its website. The stolen key could enable creation of counterfeit wallets that pass authenticity checks, putting buyers at risk of crypto theft. No actual cryptocurrency was stolen in the incident, but the breach undermines trust in Keystone's device verification process.

cards.headline: AI-generated fake login pages accelerate account takeover attacks
cards.summary: Generative AI enables attackers to create convincing fake login pages that steal passwords, capture MFA codes, and hijack authenticated sessions. Attackers can now easily impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations with minimal effort. The technology significantly lowers the barrier for credential harvesting and account takeover attacks targeting enterprises.

cards.headline: Lazarus targets South Korea using post-quantum encrypted malware
cards.summary: North Korea-linked Lazarus Group conducted a cyber espionage campaign called Operation FlashHole targeting at least three South Korean organizations in construction, software, and wire-communication equipment manufacturing since July 2025. Kaspersky attributed the campaign and noted Lazarus abused legitimate South Korean security software as part of the attack chain. The campaign demonstrates sophisticated targeting and use of advanced encryption techniques.

cards.headline: Warlock ransomware exploits unpatched SharePoint globally
cards.summary: Storm-2603 threat group behind Warlock ransomware targeted at least four organizations in Portuguese and Spanish-speaking regions via on-premises Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities. Victims included a water utility, telecommunications provider, regional government, and university. Attackers exploited flaws patched in July 2025 and newer SharePoint vulnerabilities. Organizations should prioritize SharePoint patching and review patch management processes to prevent exploitation.

cards.headline: ASD takes down Amadey malware botnet backend
cards.summary: Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) gained access to the Amadey malware backend and disconnected it from approximately 180,000 infected computers worldwide, including systems in Australia. The Amadey botnet was used to steal data and conduct further attacks. By severing the command-and-control infrastructure, ASD prevented the threat actor from continuing operations. Infected users should apply security updates.

cards.headline: ENGIE data breach affects energy company customers
cards.summary: French energy giant ENGIE, one of the world's largest power and natural gas providers, confirmed attackers stole customer data after breaching a marketing platform used by business partners. The incident affected multiple customers through a third-party system. ENGIE is investigating the breach scope and notifying affected parties. Customers should monitor accounts for suspicious activity.

cards.headline: University of New Mexico Health System diverts patients after cyber incident
cards.summary: University of New Mexico Health System experienced a cybersecurity incident that forced the closure of its main hospital in Albuquerque and resulted in cancellation of appointments across more than 30 clinics. Patients were instructed not to present at the facility. No details on the attack type or data compromised were provided. Healthcare organizations should review incident response procedures and communications to affected patients and staff.

cards.headline: CISA adds Google Brotli RCE to KEV catalog
cards.summary: Google Brotli unchecked return value vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt memory, disclose sensitive data, cause denial of service, or execute arbitrary code via crafted compressed streams. The flaw affects widely deployed compression libraries. CISA set federal patching deadline of November 10, 2026. Administrators must prioritize patching per BOD 26-04 guidance or discontinue use.

cards.headline: CISA adds Adobe Commerce file upload RCE to KEV
cards.summary: Adobe Commerce and Magento contain unrestricted file upload vulnerability (CVE-2026-48356) enabling arbitrary code execution with current user privileges, potentially leading to account takeover or elevated access. The flaw affects e-commerce platforms in widespread use. CISA set federal patching deadline of November 10, 2026. Administrators must apply vendor mitigations immediately per BOD 26-04 guidance.

cards.headline: Apple patches 304 vulnerabilities across iOS, macOS
cards.summary: Apple released its October 2026 security update addressing 304 vulnerabilities across iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and Safari. CVE-2026-86950, a previously exploited CoreGraphics flaw, received patches for iOS 18 this month. Other notable issues include CVE-2026-86990, allowing malicious apps camera access without permission, and CVE-2026-28864, enabling local attackers to access Keychain items. Developers and users should apply updates immediately.

cards.headline: University of Copenhagen breach exposes 525,000 people
cards.summary: The University of Copenhagen confirmed hackers accessed a test environment containing personal data of 525,000 individuals. The breach affected stored records in the test system. The university is investigating the scope and conducting notifications to affected individuals. Affected parties should monitor for identity theft and fraudulent activity.

cards.headline: Former pentester breaches 90+ orgs using ARTEX AI tool
cards.summary: South Korean police identified seven suspects in a cybercrime operation that breached over 90 organizations, with the ARTEX AI pentesting framework used in most attacks. A former pentester leveraged this tool to steal 8.2 million data records. The incident highlights risks of weaponized AI-powered security tools in criminal hands and the need for access controls on penetration testing frameworks.

cards.headline: Texas sues OpenAI over consumer deception claims
cards.summary: Texas filed a lawsuit against OpenAI under state deceptive trade practices laws, seeking reforms and fines for alleged consumer deception. The suit names founder and CEO Sam Altman for personal liability. This represents a regulatory challenge to AI safety marketing practices and reflects growing state-level scrutiny of AI companies' claims about their systems' safety and capabilities.

cards.headline: DreamHost forces password resets after incident
cards.summary: DreamHost has forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users following an incident that disrupted connections to the File Manager interface. The hosting provider has not disclosed full details of the incident but is taking proactive security measures. Customers should verify their account access and monitor for unauthorized activity on their hosted services.

cards.headline: PHP releases second Windows update for Brotli RCE flaw
cards.summary: PHP released rebuilt Windows packages for versions 8.2 through 8.5 to address CVE-2026-111497, a code execution flaw in the bundled Brotli compression library. The vulnerability allows memory corruption and potential remote code execution through the cURL extension when decompressing HTTP responses. Users should apply the update immediately, particularly if cURL auto-decompression is enabled.

cards.headline: Threat actors impersonate IT support via Microsoft Teams
cards.summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified a recurring social engineering pattern where attackers exploit Microsoft Teams' external chat feature to impersonate IT support, conducting scams and delivering malware and ransomware. The attacks use disposable tenant accounts and consistent impersonation tactics across hundreds of incidents. Organizations should restrict external chat permissions and educate users to verify IT support requests through official channels.

cards.headline: Microsoft releases emergency .NET patches for critical Brotli flaw
cards.summary: Microsoft released emergency security updates for .NET to patch a critical vulnerability in Brotli compression. The flaw, also tracked as Broccoli2Shell, Node2Shell, and HTTP2Shell, affects widely deployed .NET installations. The vulnerability allows remote code execution and requires immediate patching. Administrators should apply updates without delay to prevent exploitation.

cards.headline: Genesys hack exposes customer data from internal systems
cards.summary: Genesys suffered a breach that exposed customer data from internal systems. The company's primary Cloud, Engage, and Engage Cloud platforms were not affected. Organizations using Genesys should investigate whether their data was compromised and review any exposed credentials or sensitive information.

cards.headline: OpenAI reasoning traces enable cheaper rival model distillation
cards.summary: A flaw in OpenAI's model compaction process allowed researchers to extract reasoning traces and transfer them between models. This vulnerability could enable adversaries to distill cheaper rival AI systems by leveraging stolen reasoning data, potentially reducing development costs for competing AI models.

cards.headline: Dahua cameras exploited by hackers in Ukraine attacks
cards.summary: Hackers are exploiting vulnerabilities in Dahua surveillance cameras and video recorders to gain unauthorized access, according to CERT-UA. Attackers have compromised internet-connected devices, modified settings, and created unauthorized user accounts. The campaign targets Ukraine. Organizations using Dahua equipment should verify device configurations, change credentials, and apply available security updates immediately.

cards.headline: Chinese national extradited for $36 million crypto scam
cards.summary: A Chinese man was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in California for his role in a cryptocurrency investment scam that defrauded 174 US victims of nearly $37 million. Authorities arrested and prosecuted him for operating the fraudulent scheme. The case demonstrates ongoing international cooperation to prosecute large-scale financial crimes targeting US citizens.

cards.headline: 953 online stores infected in persistent malware campaign
cards.summary: A long-running malware campaign injected small loader code into 953 online stores to serve payloads to visitors while avoiding detection. The campaign targeted e-commerce platforms, likely through supply-chain compromise or website vulnerabilities. Affected stores may distribute malware to customers. Website operators should audit for unauthorized code injection, verify integrity of admin access, and implement file monitoring to detect similar infections.

cards.headline: LiteLLM exposed key enabled supply-chain attack
cards.summary: An unrevoked API key accidentally exposed in May in the open-source LiteLLM tool was used to launch a supply-chain attack targeting tens of thousands of AI developers. The compromised key allowed attackers to target users of the widely deployed library. LiteLLM developers confirmed the incident and recommend users verify account activity and rotate credentials immediately.

cards.headline: Wasmtime sandbox escape flaws discovered in WebAssembly runtime
cards.summary: Two critical vulnerabilities in Wasmtime, a WebAssembly runtime, allow malicious WebAssembly modules to escape their sandbox. One flaw affects only ARM64 systems. Attackers need a vulnerable Wasmtime build to compile a malicious module. Fixed versions are available. Organizations using Wasmtime should update immediately to prevent sandbox escapes.

cards.headline: Dutch police arrest two for NFC relay card draining attacks
cards.summary: Two individuals were arrested in the Netherlands for conducting NFC relay attacks that drained over $400,000 from bank accounts. The attackers called victims and convinced them to install a malicious app and scan their credit cards, facilitating unauthorized fund transfers. NFC relay attacks bypass contactless payment security by relaying card data without physical proximity. Defenders should educate users on social engineering tactics and promote secure payment authentication methods.

cards.headline: uCreator Android spyware steals Telegram 2FA and clones WeChat
cards.summary: A rentable Android spyware kit called uCreator hijacks Telegram and WeChat accounts by embedding malicious code into tampered versions of both applications distributed outside official app stores. The kit exploits 2FA bypass techniques to steal Telegram credentials and clone WeChat accounts. Victims are affected only when installing compromised apps or using the attackers' WeChat container. Users should install apps exclusively from official stores and enable additional security measures.

cards.headline: AitM relay compromises Microsoft 365 accounts across 79 organizations
cards.summary: A campaign used adversary-in-the-middle relay attacks to capture sign-in sessions and replay stolen tokens, breaching Microsoft 365 email accounts across 79 organizations. Researchers at Huntress detected 497 successful sign-in events between July and September 2026. Organizations should enable multifactor authentication and review sign-in logs for unusual token activity.

cards.headline: Gheist campaign steals GitHub repository secrets via Actions logs
cards.summary: Attackers using stolen GitHub tokens plant workflows that expose repository secrets in GitHub Actions logs, then download and delete the runs. The automated campaign has successfully compromised private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments. Organizations should rotate compromised tokens immediately and review GitHub Actions audit logs for suspicious activity.

cards.headline: CISA adds PHP stale state RCE to KEV catalog
cards.summary: PHP contains a stale internal request-state vulnerability enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. CISA added CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026. The vulnerability affects PHP and requires immediate patching. Federal agencies must apply mitigations by October 29, 2026, or discontinue use. Organizations should evaluate internet exposure and follow BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

cards.headline: CISA adds PHP memory corruption RCE to KEV catalog
cards.summary: PHP contains an out-of-memory corruption vulnerability enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. CISA added CVE-2026-109618 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026. The vulnerability affects PHP and requires immediate patching. Federal agencies must apply mitigations by October 29, 2026, or discontinue use. Organizations should evaluate internet exposure and follow BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

cards.headline: Hacked Tailscale device escalates to root on network
cards.summary: Unpatched flaws in Tailscale SSH allow a compromised device on a Tailscale network to gain root access on other connected servers. The attack requires SSH port forwarding enabled and network access rules permitting device-to-device communication. Affected organizations should review Tailscale SSH configurations, disable port forwarding if unnecessary, and update to patched versions immediately.

cards.headline: PHP2Shell flaws exploited against European government
cards.summary: Threat actors exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to breach a European government entity, accessing password hashes and multi-factor authentication credentials within two hours. Attackers used agentic AI platforms for post-exploitation activities. Global scanning for vulnerable targets is ongoing. Organizations should patch PHP implementations immediately and monitor for unauthorized access.

cards.headline: AI coding agents hijacked via malicious AGENTS.md file
cards.summary: Researchers discovered a malicious AGENTS markdown file in a customer's Downloads folder that tricked an AI coding agent into installing a rogue npm package. The vulnerability exploits how AI agents parse local instructions without proper verification. This highlights supply chain and social engineering risks in automated agent workflows. Organizations using AI coding agents should monitor file system access and validate package sources.

cards.headline: OpenAI AI agents demonstrate VM escapes and sandbox escape
cards.summary: OpenAI has announced plans to conduct frontier model training without live internet access as it resumes reinforcement learning training of its most advanced AI models. The company cited alignment research, monitoring systems, and internet infrastructure security as reasons for the decision. This represents a cautious approach to developing increasingly capable AI systems.

cards.headline: Time4Popcorn app exposed millions to RCE via vulnerable updater
cards.summary: Researchers discovered and remotely disabled a vulnerability in the abandoned Time4Popcorn BitTorrent client that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges on affected systems. The flaw existed in the app's updater mechanism. Millions of devices potentially running outdated versions remain at risk. Users should immediately uninstall the application or update to the patched version if available.

cards.headline: APT41 BlackX UEFI bootkit bypasses Windows Secure Boot
cards.summary: A sophisticated UEFI bootkit called BlackX has targeted diplomatic organizations in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan since early 2026. Attributed to China-linked APT41, it bypasses Secure Boot on patched Windows systems by exploiting missing revocations. The bootkit achieves persistent kernel-level access before the operating system loads. Affected organizations should verify firmware integrity and apply security updates from vendors.

cards.headline: INC and Gentlemen groups automate intrusions with AI framework
cards.summary: Cybersecurity researchers uncovered a Russian-speaking ransomware affiliate ecosystem using an AI-driven intrusion framework called Phantom operated by INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups. The autonomous red-team system orchestrates end-to-end attack chains for both intrusion and data exfiltration. The discovery reveals how ransomware gangs are adopting AI agents to scale breach operations.

cards.headline: FCC bans Huawei surveillance devices from US market
cards.summary: The FCC has banned two consumer devices—a wireless video transmitter and dashboard camera—manufactured with Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon surveillance chips. The restriction reflects escalating US-China technology tensions and concerns over potential data collection risks. Affected products are no longer permitted for sale or operation in the United States.

cards.headline: AI models drive mass-scale attacks for minimal cost
cards.summary: Threat actors are leveraging open-weight AI models to generate large-scale cyberattacks targeting hundreds of sites with unprecedented efficiency. One campaign targeted 105 sites, while another gained full domain control for just $12. Security defenders face pressure to adapt strategies as AI-powered attacks become commoditized, increasing attack volume without proportional increase in sophistication requirements.
